cards.explanation: The answer is the chief priests and scribes, friends. Jesus says the Son of Man will be delivered over to the chief priests and scribes (Matthew 20:18). He says it plain, with no sprinkles on top to make it prettier. I think the Twelve got quiet real fast after that.

The answer is True, and Jesus says it Himself. He tells the Twelve, "They will condemn Him to death" (Matthew 20:18). He's not hinting or dropping a riddle here. He lays it out ahead of time, which tells me He knows exactly where this road goes.

The answer is Gentiles, friends, the non-Jewish nations. Jesus says they will "…deliver Him over to the Gentiles…" (Matthew 20:19). So He's handed over first to the chief priests and scribes, and then on to the Gentiles. Jesus lays out the whole order before it happens.

The answer is that He will be raised to life, and this is the best part of the whole announcement. Jesus says, "…on the third day He will be raised to life." (Matthew 20:19). He mentions the hard things, and then He tells them it doesn't end there. Always read to the end of the sentence, friends.

The answer is one at His right and one at His left, friends. She says, "Declare that in Your kingdom one of these two sons of mine may sit at Your right hand, and the other at Your left." (Matthew 20:21). Those are the two seats right beside Jesus, and she wants her sons in both of them. She walked in with a very specific request, I'll give her that.

The answer is "We can," friends. The brothers answer, "We can" (Matthew 20:22). Jesus had asked if they could drink the cup He was going to drink. I think they had no idea how big that cup was. Jesus follows up and says they will indeed drink His cup (Matthew 20:23).

The answer is False, friends. Jesus tells the two brothers, "You will indeed drink My cup…" (Matthew 20:23). They had said "We can" when He asked if they could drink the cup He was going to drink (Matthew 20:22), and He tells them yes, they will. Only the seats are left open, because those aren't His to grant.
The answer is Father, friends. Jesus says, "These seats belong to those for whom My Father has prepared them." (Matthew 20:23). So it's the Father who has prepared them, and Jesus says so plainly.

The answer is indignant, friends. The ten "…were indignant with the two brothers." (Matthew 20:24). That means they were stirred up and not happy about what was asked. The request came from the mother of Zebedee's sons, and the ten were indignant with her sons.

The answer is True, friends. Jesus says, "You know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them…" (Matthew 20:25). He's pointing at how rulers act so He can show a different way. And that different way is coming in the very next verse.

The answer is servant, friends, and what a flip that is. Jesus says, "…whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant…" (Matthew 20:26). Greatness shows up as serving. It's the opposite of lording it over people.

The answer is to serve and give His life as a ransom for many, and it's the heart of the whole passage. Jesus says the Son of Man came "…to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many." (Matthew 20:28). Right before that, He says whoever wants to become great among them must be their servant.
